  • Algeria Cleanroom

    • Algeria Cleanroom 

    Algeria has the second largest pharmaceutical market in Africa. 

    1. The pros and cons of drugs are not only directly reflected in the efficacy and safety, but also in the stability, consistency and practicality of the drugs. 
    2. In order to ensure the quality of medicines, in addition to complying with relevant legal standards such as pharmacopoeia, it is very important to carry out production in a clean environment.
    3. Hazardous or non-hazardous foreign matter in the air of the production area should be minimized, and HVAC system will supply sufficient air to remove airborne particulates that may contaminate the product.
    4. The manufacturing process of sterile preparations consists of clean room areas from 10,000 to 100 level. 

    Clean room is an integral part of the manufacturing process required to produce sterile drug products, vaccines and bio-medical devices. 

    What do we do for Algeria Cleanroom Industry

    RV-Cleanroom who has been a turnkey solution provider to the pharmaceutical manufacturing industry since 2002.

    We provide a quality clean room project of pharmaceutical professionals with international standard capabilities.

    Our pharmaceutical consultants can offer practical knowledge and experience on implementing or enhancing your Pharmaceutical Quality Systems (PQS) to meet GMP code requirements and those based on ICH Q10 / ISO 9001:2015 for Pharmaceuticals.

    RV-Cleanroom modular cleanrooms are built with own modular panels. It is assembled on site. Our factory enables us to produce and guarantee product quality and on-time delivery. 

    With 20 years of experience in the industry RV-Cleanroom has assisted many clients in various industries by providing air treatment solutions.

CLEANROOM

  • China Cleanroom Manufacturer & factory
  • CLEANROOM

    • CLEANROOM

    History of Clean Room Technology

    Rooted in the control of infections in hospitals.

    Clean rooms for industrial manufacturing started during the second world war

    An attempt to improve the quality and reliablility of instrumentation used in guns, tanks and aircraft.

    Industrial Clean Room

    Semiconductor

    Cleanroom technoloty of paramount important to create and ideal semiconducting material and chemical purity. Any small imperfection can have a drastic effect on how the semiconducting material behaves due to the scale at which the materials are used.
    This industry drives the state-of-the art clean room design, and this industry accounts for a significant number of all operating clean rooms.

    Pharmaceutical

    Cleanroom is an integral part of the manufacturing process required to produce sterile drug products, vaccines and bio-medical devices. Clean rooms control living particles that would produce undesirable bacterial growth in the preparation of biological, pharmaceutical, and other medical products as well as in genetic engineering research.

    Miscellaneous Applications

    Other uses include advanced materials research, laser and optic industries, microelectronices facility, paint room and some aseptic foods production. While hospital operating rooms can be considered clean spaces, their concern is to control types of contamination rather than the quantity of particles present.

    External Sources of Contamination

    Primarily through the air conditioning system

    Infiltrate through building doors, windows, cracks

    Controlled primarily by 1. High efficiency filtration 2. Space pressuriation 3.Sealing of space penetrations

    Internal Sources of Contamination

    Largest source is from people

    Shedding of surfaces, process equipment and the process itself

    Controlled primarilly by 1. Airflow design 2. Careful selection of materials & equipment 3. Personal garments

How to Choose a Reliable Chinese Cleanroom Supplier for Your Project

  • China Cleanroom Manufacturer & factory
  • How to Choose a Reliable Chinese Cleanroom Supplier for Your Project

    • Choosing the right Chinese cleanroom supplier is one of the most important decisions in any cleanroom project. Many buyers first compare prices, but low pricing alone does not guarantee cleanroom performance, compliance, or long-term reliability. A poorly designed or poorly installed cleanroom can lead to contamination risks, failed inspections, production delays, and costly rework.

    Whether you are planning a china cleanroom facility for pharmaceutical production, medical devices, electronics, laboratories, or food processing, it is essential to evaluate suppliers based on engineering capability, manufacturing quality, compliance knowledge, and after-sales support. A reliable Chinese turn-key cleanroom project supplier should not only manufacture panels and equipment, but also understand airflow control, pressure differentials, material flow, personnel flow, and validation requirements.

    This guide explains what buyers should check before choosing a dependable Chinese cleanroom supplier.

    1. Define Your Cleanroom Requirements Clearly

    Before contacting any supplier, you should first define your technical and operational requirements. Clear input helps suppliers prepare an accurate design, quotation, and project scope. Vague requirements often lead to unsuitable layouts, budget overruns, and project delays.

    Cleanroom Classification

    Start by identifying the required cleanroom standard, such as ISO 14644 or GMP. The target cleanroom class affects filtration, air change rates, room pressure, airflow pattern, and testing requirements. For example, an ISO 8 cleanroom has very different design requirements from an ISO 5 or GMP critical area.

    Industry Application

    Different industries require different cleanroom solutions. Pharmaceutical cleanrooms may require GMP-focused layouts, smooth hygienic finishes, pressure cascade control, and validation support. Electronics cleanrooms may require tighter particle control and static protection. Food and laboratory cleanrooms may need specific hygiene zoning, washable surfaces, and controlled personnel entry.

    Layout and Workflow

    A supplier should also understand your room dimensions, process flow, equipment layout, and future expansion plans. A good cleanroom design is not just about walls and ceilings. It must also support efficient personnel movement, material transfer, maintenance access, and contamination control.

    2. Check Certifications and Compliance Knowledge

    A qualified Chinese cleanroom supplier should be able to demonstrate real knowledge of cleanroom compliance, not just mention standards in marketing materials.

    ISO and GMP Experience

    Ask whether the supplier has experience with ISO-classified and GMP-related cleanroom projects. They should understand how cleanroom classification affects room construction, HVAC design, filtration stages, and validation.

    Material and Component Documentation

    A professional supplier should be able to provide technical documentation for cleanroom panels, doors, windows, HEPA filters, lighting, flooring, and HVAC components. These documents may include material specifications, certificates, datasheets, and test reports. Proper documentation is important for inspection, approval, and long-term traceability.

    Testing and Validation Support

    Reliable suppliers should also understand cleanroom testing and commissioning. Depending on the project, this may include particle count testing, airflow velocity measurement, pressure differential checks, temperature and humidity verification, illumination testing, and noise measurement. For regulated industries, validation support is a major advantage.

    3. Review Real Project Experience

    A supplier’s past projects can tell you far more than a product catalog. Cleanroom projects involve design coordination, manufacturing accuracy, logistics, site installation, and system commissioning. Experience matters.

    Relevant Industry Portfolio

    Review the supplier’s project portfolio and check whether they have experience in industries similar to yours. A company that has delivered pharmaceutical, laboratory, medical device, food, or electronics cleanrooms is more likely to understand industry-specific requirements.

    Project Scale and Complexity

    It is also important to know whether the supplier has handled projects of similar size and complexity. A company that can supply a small clean booth may not be capable of managing a full turnkey cleanroom with HVAC, utility coordination, and overseas installation.

    Modular Project Capability

    If you are evaluating a Chinese modular cleanroom manufacturer, ask whether they have completed a similar modular cleanroom project in China or in export markets. Modular cleanrooms require accurate production, clean interfaces, fast installation, and the flexibility to expand later.

    Client References

    Ask for client references, project photos, case studies, or installation records. These materials help verify whether the supplier has real delivery experience rather than only trading activity.

    4. Evaluate Factory and Manufacturing Capability

    One of the biggest advantages of working with a Chinese cleanroom supplier can be manufacturing capacity, but buyers still need to verify whether the supplier has real in-house production control.

    In-House Cleanroom Panel Production

    If the supplier produces cleanroom wall and ceiling panels in-house, this usually improves consistency and quality control. This is especially important when reviewing cleanroom panels manufacture China capability, because panel accuracy affects sealing, appearance, and installation speed.

    HVAC and Filtration Capability

    A cleanroom is not just a panel enclosure. Its performance depends heavily on HVAC design, filtration, airflow balance, and pressure control. Ask whether the supplier can provide AHU selection, ductwork planning, HEPA terminal layout, air change rate calculations, and pressure cascade design. A supplier without HVAC engineering capability may only be selling construction materials, not a full cleanroom solution.

    Customization and Modular Design

    A strong supplier should be able to customize room size, panel type, windows, doors, return air walls, pass boxes, air showers, and equipment integration based on your layout. This is one of the main advantages of choosing a modular cleanroom manufacturer China with proven engineering support. Modular cleanroom capability is especially important if you may expand or adjust the facility in the future.

    5. Ask What Documents the Supplier Can Provide

    Professional documentation is often a clear sign that you are dealing with a serious cleanroom company.

    A reliable Chinese cleanroom supplier should typically be able to provide documents such as:

    1.  Cleanroom layout drawings

    2.  Panel and material specifications

    3.  HVAC schematic or airflow design basis

    4.  Equipment datasheets

    5.  BOQ or itemized quotation

    6.  Installation drawings

    7.  Operation and maintenance manuals

    8.  Testing or commissioning records

    9.  Material certificates and filter data

    These documents are especially important in any china cleanroom turn-key project, where owners, consultants, contractors, and inspectors may all need to review the same technical scope.

    6. Assess Installation and Overseas Project Support

    Even high-quality cleanroom materials can fail if installation is poor. Alignment errors, sealing defects, weak joint treatment, or improper HVAC balancing can affect cleanroom performance and compliance.

    On-Site Installation Team

    Check whether the supplier has its own installation team or only outsources site work. Directly managed installation is often more reliable, especially for modular cleanrooms, air showers, pass boxes, doors, and ceiling systems that require precise assembly.

    Commissioning and Handover

    A dependable supplier should support commissioning, system checks, and project handover. This is especially important for overseas projects, where clients may need remote guidance, installation supervision, or startup assistance.

    After-Sales Service

    Long-term support also matters. Ask whether the supplier can provide spare parts, filter replacement guidance, remote troubleshooting, maintenance recommendations, and technical support after project completion.

    7. Compare Value, Not Just Price

    Many buyers choose a Chinese cleanroom supplier because of cost advantages, but the lowest quotation is not always the best value. Some low-priced offers exclude important items such as HVAC, installation, commissioning, testing, or validation support.

    Detailed Quotation Breakdown

    Ask for itemized pricing that clearly separates cleanroom panels, doors, windows, HVAC systems, cleanroom equipment, installation, shipping, and optional services. A transparent quotation reduces the chance of hidden costs later.

    Scope Definition

    Make sure the supplier clearly defines what is included and excluded. For example, does the quotation include only materials, or does it also include design, installation, commissioning, and validation assistance?

    Payment Terms and Milestones

    Professional suppliers usually offer structured payment milestones linked to project progress, manufacturing, shipment, and installation stages. Clear payment terms help protect both parties and reduce misunderstandings.

    8. Watch for Common Warning Signs

    Before selecting a Chinese cleanroom supplier, buyers should also watch for red flags.

    Common warning signs include:

    1.  No real factory or production photos

    2.  No engineering team for HVAC and cleanroom design

    3.  Very low prices with unclear scope

    4.  Limited documentation or missing certificates

    5.  No overseas project experience

    6.  No testing or commissioning support

    7.  No installation supervision capability

    8.  Slow or unclear technical communication

    A reliable supplier should be transparent, technically responsive, and able to explain solutions clearly.

    9. Questions Buyers Should Ask Before Ordering

    To reduce project risk, buyers should ask a few practical questions before making a final decision:

    1.  Have you completed projects similar to ours?

    2.  Can you provide project photos or case studies?

    3.  Do you manufacture cleanroom panels in-house?

    4.  Can you design the HVAC system and airflow layout?

    5.  What standards do your cleanrooms follow?

    6.  Can you provide drawings, datasheets, and certificates?

    7.  Do you support overseas installation or supervision?

    8.  Can you assist with commissioning and cleanroom testing?

    9.  What is included in your quotation?

    These questions help identify whether the supplier is only selling products or can actually deliver a complete cleanroom solution.

    10. Buyer Checklist: What to Verify Before Choosing a Supplier

    Final Thoughts

    Choosing a reliable Chinese cleanroom supplier requires more than comparing prices. Buyers should evaluate technical capability, manufacturing control, compliance knowledge, documentation, installation support, and real project experience. A dependable supplier should be able to support your project from design and production to installation, commissioning, and long-term service.

    When selected carefully, a professional Chinese cleanroom supplier can offer strong manufacturing capacity, flexible modular solutions, competitive pricing, and dependable project delivery for international clients.

     

    Looking for a trusted Chinese cleanroom supplier?

    Frequently Asked Questions

    Is it safe to buy a cleanroom from China?

    Yes, it can be safe and cost-effective if you choose a supplier with real factory capacity, technical documentation, project references, and installation support. The key is to verify engineering capability and project experience, not just compare price.

    How can I verify a Chinese cleanroom supplier?

    Ask for factory photos, workshop videos, project case studies, technical drawings, product datasheets, material certificates, and client references. You should also check whether the supplier can explain HVAC design, cleanroom classification, and commissioning procedures clearly.

    What should a cleanroom quotation include?

    A professional quotation should clearly list cleanroom panels, doors, windows, HVAC systems, Power system, cleanroom equipment, optional installation, shipping, and commissioning scope. It should also explain what is included and excluded.

    Why is HVAC expertise important when choosing a cleanroom supplier?

    A cleanroom depends on controlled airflow, filtration, pressure differentials, temperature, and humidity. Without proper HVAC design, even high-quality panels and equipment cannot deliver stable cleanroom performance.

    Can a Chinese cleanroom supplier support overseas projects?

    Many experienced suppliers can support overseas projects through remote design coordination, factory production, shipment planning, installation supervision, commissioning support, and after-sales service. Buyers should confirm this capability before ordering.

The amount of negative ions in the air of the cleanroom

  • China Cleanroom Manufacturer & factory
  • The amount of negative ions in the air of the cleanroom

    • Generally, ions in the air are divided into three categories: small ions, medium ions and large ions.Small ions are complexes composed of 3-12 molecules with basic charges; medium ions are complexes composed of about 100-1000 molecules, generally deposited on microparticles; large ions are composed of 106 molecules aggregated together the condensed nucleus.

    Effects of negative ions in the air on the human body

    In fact, negative ions are negatively charged molecules in the air, and negative oxygen ions are negatively charged oxygen molecules. produced by air ionization. In nature, there are many negative ions in the air of forests, waterfalls, and seaside. There is a tourist attraction in some city that is famous for its negative ions. The content of negative ions in the air is as high as 200,000-300,000/cm3.

    Practice has proved that the negative ions in the air have certain physiological effects on the human body, which are manifested in: lowering blood pressure, inhibiting asthma, calming nerves, eliminating fatigue, enhancing the body's immunity and antibacterial ability, making people feel refreshed and working efficiently. Experiments have shown that when the negative ions in the air come into contact with the respiratory organs, charge migration occurs and stimulates the organs. The lighter the ions, the stronger the activity, and the more obvious the stimulation to the organs. The result of this biological stimulation will provide the content of free oxygen in the human blood, which will increase the amount of carbon dioxide exhaled and oxygen inhaled by the human body, which means that it has certain benefits for the human body.

    The air in the clean room is filtered by pre, medium and high efficiency filters, so the negative ions content in the clean room air is almost zero. It is also one reason why people feel uncomfortable in cleanrooms.

    Therefore, negative ions are not only needed in daily life, but also in clean rooms.
